newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila market rise reflect faith in economic gains.
newsitem.headline: Manila market rise reflect faith in economic gains.

text.p: Philippine Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said on Thursday that the stock market's record closing high reflected investor confidence that the country's economic gains can be sustained.

"The market is a parameter of the people's perception of the Philippine economy. We just posted growth rates that were higher than last year showing therefore that the sustainable growth that President (Fidel) Ramos has been aiming for continues," said de Ocampo in a television interview.

Stock market analysts said that the market's run-up on Thursday to an all-time high of 3,404.80 and a record closing high of 3,392.76 points were in part inspired by release of 1996 Gross National Product (GNP) growth figures that were within expectations.
The National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA) announced on Wednesday that the 1996 GNP growth of 6.8 percent was within the government's forecast of 6.5-7.5 percent for the entire year.
"The fact that we are reaching record levels that we have not attained before indicates that there's a lot of confidence by the investing community in the Philippine economy," de Ocampo said.
The finance official added that lower inflation rates, higher investment and export rates are signs that the Philippine's economic gains are sustainable.
